title: Temple of Apollo, Pompeii
visualBrief: Specific standing Apollo sanctuary at Pompeii: roofless raised podium/cella with two tall fluted front columns and varied broken stumps, frontal pale/brick stair, separate pale altar with rolled ends and sundial column; surrounding open court has surviving/broken fluted portico shafts and a short east entablature, rough enclosing walls and an original simplified volumetric bronze replica figure. No restored temple roof/pediment, broad precinct slab or copied sculpture/text atlas.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained exact-QID ruins-area way240573968/Q2699249 fixes the55.1x34.4m precinct boundary, not the temple building footprint. Named standard PMTiles point35184612662800 and central occupied altar-like control35185565970074 correlate the sanctuary. Anchor14.484426935,40.749212932; heading0, internal cross-axis-.444299136394rad, front toward south/southeast local+z. Internal podium/cella/column allocation is ordinary-picture-led within the mapped precinct. Other independent mapped structures including northeast corner control35185565970071 remain native.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Picture/map estimates only: central podium12.5x22m with its upper floor2.4m above anchor DEM datum; roofless cella6.8x12.8m, surviving walls1.4-2.6m above podium, front columns6.3m above podium and varied0.6-1.8m stumps. Frontal stair6m wide with16steps. Court side rows12 stations each and end rows5 intermediate stations each: original simplified approximate survival inventory, not an archaeological survey. Short east four-column entablature about4.6m above local floor. Altar2.8x1.55m, sundial4.7m high, replica figure1.75m. Hidden wall/column inventories and precise capital/repair details approximate.
